data.text: Marcus, this is Klein from cardiology pharmacy. I am calling to make sure the new metoprolol dose is clear.

prior_context.speaker: clinician_dr_patel
prior_context.text: Correct. Also do not miss any apixaban doses at all between now and cardioversion.

prior_context.speaker: agent_memcare
prior_context.text: Cardiology plan update: continue apixaban 5 mg BID without interruption, increase metoprolol tartrate to 37.5 mg BID starting tonight, stop ibuprofen/NSAIDs, use acetaminophen if needed, start magnesium oxide 400 mg nightly for five nights, continue lisinopril 10 mg daily but hold morning dose on procedure day.

prior_context.speaker: labtech_mira
prior_context.text: Your labs are back: hemoglobin 14.1, potassium 4.1, magnesium 1.7, creatinine 1.0, and TSH 1.9.

prior_context.speaker: clinician_dr_patel
prior_context.text: Those labs are acceptable for outpatient cardioversion, and the magnesium result supports the supplement plan we just discussed.

prior_context.speaker: scheduler_terry
prior_context.text: I just got a tentative slot. Direct cardioversion is being held for Wednesday, March 11 at 10:20 AM with 8:50 AM arrival in the cardiac procedures unit.

prior_context.speaker: scheduler_terry
prior_context.text: Prep for that slot would be nothing by mouth after midnight except small sips of water for approved morning medications. We will confirm whether that slot stays direct cardioversion or changes to a TEE-guided case.

prior_context.speaker: patient_marcus_reed
prior_context.text: Please put that in the chart, and Nina can hear only the Wednesday time and arrival window, nothing about the medication plan.

prior_context.speaker: family_nina_reed
prior_context.text: All I need is whether I should block off Wednesday morning.

prior_context.speaker: scheduler_terry
prior_context.text: At the moment, yes: Wednesday morning, 8:50 arrival for a 10:20 procedure. Any clinical questions need to go through Marcus.

prior_context.speaker: agent_memcare
prior_context.text: Scheduling note: logistics-only family access still active through Monday. Current tentative slot is Wednesday March 11, 8:50 AM arrival for 10:20 AM procedure in cardiac procedures.

states.content: Cardioversion remains the plan for Marcus Reed's atrial fibrillation rhythm control. A tentative slot is being held for direct cardioversion on Wednesday, March 11 at 10:20 AM, with 8:50 AM arrival in the cardiac procedures unit; this slot is tentative and not yet confirmed with the patient or procedures unit. Marcus requests that the tentative Wednesday slot details be put in the chart. The scheduler will confirm whether that slot stays direct cardioversion or changes to a TEE-guided case. Dr. Patel has reviewed the labs and stated they are acceptable for outpatient cardioversion, satisfying the pending-labs condition; full medication history reconciliation remains part of the plan. Dr. Patel instructs that Marcus must not miss any apixaban doses at all between now and cardioversion. Nurse Jamison will bring Marcus back first for his cardiology rhythm clinic visit, and Nina can be updated on arrival windows if Marcus keeps the logistics-only setting active. As of the latest update, Marcus is still being evaluated and no final arrival time has been set; Nina asked at the desk whether the timing changed, and Jamison told her only that Marcus is still being evaluated with no final arrival time set.

states.content: Nurse Jamison is reviewing Marcus Reed's medications exactly as he is taking them right now, to prepare an accurate current medication list. Marcus reported taking ibuprofen a couple of times last week for shoulder pain before remembering he probably should not with the blood thinner (apixaban). Dr. Patel has now instructed Marcus to stop ibuprofen and other NSAIDs and to use acetaminophen instead if needed, because NSAIDs raise bleeding risk with apixaban. Marcus reported he has not missed any morning apixaban doses and no completely missed doses in the last three weeks as far as he remembers; he might have been a few hours late last Monday night when changing locations but still took that pill before bed. Nurse Jamison will document the Monday-night apixaban dose as possibly delayed but not skipped. Marcus does not drink energy drinks.
